correctness.rationale: For every n>=3, an unchosen edge-subdivision cycle is permanently unobservable; when its residual graph is a forest, all original vertices become observed (including the no-initial-original star case), and leaf forcing empties the forest. Counting forests yields every coefficient; the sharp forest edge bound leaves exactly the two optimum types. The exchange proof gives explicit Johnson-shortest paths for all three type-pair cases, proves degree/edge/eccentricity formulae and supplies a four-symbol basis-exchange obstruction. check_forest.cpp exhaustively tests all initial sets through n=6 (2,097,152 at n=6). Independently check_enumerator.py simulates propagation and enumerates forests through n=5 and independently reconstructs complete exchange graphs and all-pairs distances through n=9. Neither finite test is substituted for the all-order proof.

value.rationale: The natural full one-edge subdivision of a clique models observation from original vertices and monitored edges. An exact forest criterion gives the entire family of feasible monitoring placements. The sharp optimum has two intrinsic, geometrically different types and a closed labeled count. The reconfiguration network is nonetheless Johnson-isometric for all n, even as matroid exchange fails: this is a strong and reusable counterexample to conflating shortest token-jump accessibility with matroid structure. The degree formulas and sharp radius/diameter transition quantify sensor replacement robustness. This is a structural infinite-family theorem rather than an arbitrary enumeration.
